title: Vladimir Putin, a president sealed off in a Russia under lockdown
subhead: 'The Putin System' (1/3). The many 'siloviki,' officers drawn from Russia's security services, have seized power and are now omnipresent among the country's elites. Within society, they have spread an atmosphere of fear and suspicion that prohibits any questioning of the Kremlin or its war in Ukraine.

subhead: The report by the Office of the Inspector General (OIG) of the Department of Homeland Security (DHS) found that between July 2025 and January 2026, 79 detainees were confined in the small enclosures for periods ranging from several minutes to nearly two hours.

title: 'The growing debate over the 'AIpocalypse' is also, and above all, about big money'
subhead: As leaders in the artificial intelligence sector warn of the existential risks posed by their own technology, Anthropic prepares for the largest IPO in history. In his column, Le Monde's New York correspondent, Nicolas Chapuis, explores this dangerous paradox.

Wide open for other candidates, the race is drawing significant interest from voters concerned about the future, Le Monde's first poll shows.

title: Céline Dion returns to stage for first Paris show: 'I want to sing for you, to sing about life'
subhead: With a controlled voice and a relatively understated show, the Québécois star delighted the 30,000 spectators at the Plenitude Arena just outside the French capital with a 25-song set over two hours and 15 minutes. It was her first concert in six years.

title: On the shores of the Strait of Hormuz, an Iranian photographer captures the lives caught between sea and fire: 'It was necessary to show what war does to them'
subhead: On the Iranian islands along this strategic passage, the war between the US and Iran has upended the lives of fishers, merchants and families connected to both shores of the Persian Gulf. The consequences are captured in photographs by one Iranian – whose identity has been concealed for security reasons.
